name: Yucca — all Kew-accepted species
status: 4 archetypal species (full list archived in docs/plant_archive)
notes: All 55 species accepted by Kew POWO (hybrids dropped). Nearly the whole genus is North American dry country: Mojave/Sonoran/Chihuahuan deserts, the Great Plains, Texas limestone, the Mexican plateau, plus a few SE-US dune species and one Chiapas rainforest epiphyte. Yucca moths are the only pollinator; where insects are absent it spreads by rhizome offsets only. Tree forms use the gnarled shape (Phase 6 should give the cactus/gnarled builder a dagger-crown option); rosettes use spike_rosette, which exists.

shrub.name: Spanish bayonet

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a long thin cotyledon, then a small stemless rosette of narrow, soft green leaves that get stiffer with each flush. Within a few years the rosette rises on a short trunk and the leaves become rigid dark green daggers with needle-sharp tips and finely toothed edges; dead leaves hang down the stem, and suckers from the base build a clump of trunks.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Yucca aloifolia): 1.5-6.1 m, trunks 7.6-12.7 cm thick, leaves about 0.6 m, coastal dune sands; NC State Extension plant toolbox: 3-4.5 m, slow-growing, full sun (in shade leaves are small and it rarely blooms). Germination, growth curve, first flowering and lifespan estimated from related yuccas.

shrub.name: Joshua tree

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings nearly always come up in the shade of a nurse shrub such as blackbrush: a thin grassy cotyledon, then about 4 narrow leaves by three weeks, adding roughly one leaf every 2 months. For years it is a small stemless spiky rosette of blue-green daggers; then an unbranched trunk rises a few cm a year, clothed in dead down-turned leaves, until first flowering at 1-3 m makes it branch.
growth.source: USDA FEIS (Yucca brevifolia): 100% germination in 1-5 days at 20-25 C, 22-day seedlings have about 4 leaves, one new leaf every 2 months, 7.6 cm/yr for 10 yr then 3.8 cm/yr, established after 3-5 yr, 93% of seedlings under nurse shrubs, unbranched until 0.9-3 m, average life 150 yr, large trees 300 yr. First-flowering age derived from these rates.

Fruit set, crop, hang and rot estimated.

shrub.name: Izote

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings form a small stemless rosette of soft, flat 'embryonic' leaves that last at least a year; from 4-6 months these start being replaced by stiffer leaves, and from 18 months to 3 years the plant carries only rigid, straight, dark green leaves whose edges peel into curly white threads. The single trunk rises slowly and branches only after flowering, becoming a many-armed tree.
growth.source: Spanish Wikipedia (Yucca filifera): over 10 m and, when old, up to 40 branches; leaves to 55 x 3.6 cm; flowers late April to late May; 60-80% germination (viability about 48%); embryonic leaves last at least a year, replaced from 4-6 months, fully adult leaves from 18 months to 3 years. Growth rate, first flowering and lifespan estimated.

shrub.name: Soapweed yucca

growth.juvenile_note: Germinates within days in warm moist soil: a long thin cotyledon, then a small rosette of narrow, soft, grass-like leaves. Seedlings grow slower than offsets; over several years the rosette becomes a dense stemless tuft of narrow, stiff, blue-green, sharp-tipped leaves edged in white with fine curling threads, on a deep taproot and rhizomes that sprout new rosettes.
growth.source: USDA FEIS (Yucca glauca): 50% germination in 6 days, 4 days after soaking at 27-32 C, up to 91%; seedlings grow slower than ramets; to 1 m, leaves 20-100 cm, roots over 6 m deep, rhizomes 10-60 cm deep; takes several years to bloom. Size curve (rosette spread), first flowering and rosette lifespan estimated.
